name: Murloc
summary: Along Azeroth's shores, lakes, and rivers, Murloc tribes gather and press inland from the deep ocean. Their cries and sudden swarms make them a threat, yet their deeds hint at minds sharper than their looks suggest.

sections.title: Creatures of the Shallows
sections.body: Murlocs gather along coasts, riverbanks, and freshwater lakes. They stand about four feet tall, with bulbous bodies coated in slime and wide mouths full of sharp fangs. Their keen sight pierces pitch-black water, and few stray far from their kin. Where one appears, a dozen more may wait below the surface. Together, they overwhelm foes with numbers and crude, sharp weapons.

sections.title: The Inland March
sections.body: Ancient lineages say Murlocs lived beneath the waves before recorded history. Their spread onto Lordaeron and Kalimdor is recent, and began suspiciously alongside the naga's return from the ocean depths. Some tribes appear to worship monstrous beings in the deepest reaches. They may be fleeing darker terrors, or preparing the world for their masters' awakening. Their movement into freshwaters grows more coordinated, and more dangerous.

sections.title: A Hidden Intellect
sections.body:
Outsiders hear bubbling Murloc speech and mistake it for nonsense, dismissing them as feral pests. Yet their ambushes are coordinated, and they practice earth and water magic and live in communities. Explorer Brann Bronzebeard has suggested they hide their cunning and are far smarter than civilized races realize.

Murlocs have shaped history, too. Their raid on the Darkspear tribe brought Thrall to intervene. That intervention forged the bond between orcs and trolls that built the modern Horde.

faq.q: Why do murlocs attack all at once?
faq.answer: Murlocs rarely fight alone. Their crowded settlements answer intruders together, swarming them with overwhelming numbers.

Yes. Murlocs are far more intelligent than their comical appearance suggests. Most outsiders cannot understand their guttural, gurgling speech, but Murlocs make weapons, plan ambushes, and wield water and earth magic. Brann Bronzebeard believes they let others underestimate their minds.

faq.q: Why are murlocs moving inland from the sea?
faq.answer: Murlocs once lived on the ocean floor and have steadily spread into freshwater lakes and riverbeds. Historians suspect the naga's return or deep-sea beings sleeping in the abyss may have driven them inland. Those entities' awakening commands the Murlocs to secure the land.

faq.q: How did murlocs help form the Horde?
faq.answer: During the Third War, Murlocs serving the sea witch Zar'jira ambushed the Darkspear trolls on their island home. Warchief Thrall and his orc warriors joined Sen'jin to defend them. The battle forged a lasting bond between orcs and the Darkspear tribe, laying the foundation of the modern Horde.
Mur'gul are Murlocs encountered during the Third War. Despite their strange appearance and name, they are living creatures.

faq.q: What is that iconic sound murlocs make?
faq.answer: When hunting or sounding an alarm, Murlocs make a loud, wet, wavering gargle, often rendered as “Aaaaaughibbrgubugbugrguburgle” or “RwlRwlRwlRwl.” The sound can unsettle foes and call their pack to gather.

angles.text: The Darkspear tribe has a bitter history with Murlocs. Coastal tribes captured Darkspear trolls for ritual sacrifice before the tribe joined Warchief Thrall.
Thrall's warriors fought Murlocs while rescuing the Darkspear trolls at sea. They learned early that a comical appearance can hide savage brutality.
Settlers across Westfall, Darkshore, and Lakeshire often find Murloc tribes besieging their shipping, farms, and docks.
Murloc mystics have a crude, innate bond with water and earth elementals. They bend local spirits to strengthen their shoreline villages.
